text:
maya: Nightly eval alert: big quality drop on redwood-6b-quant for cs-suite, metric down 0.62->0.27. Seen around 03:41 — lots of prompt failures and weird repeats. @liam @nora please triage :eyes:
liam: On it. Any failing examples or repro commands?
maya: Example snippet: Prompt ID cs-482 -> output repeats invented dates. Repro command: `python eval.py --model redwood-6b-quant --seed 42 --temp 0.8 --top_p 0.95`
nora: Nightly config should be temp=0.7/top_p=0.9 by default. Did anyone change quantization or eval prompts?
maya: No prompt changes. CI diffs clean. But runtime deploy yesterday included a sampler tweak (PR #2896). Might be related.
sasha: Pulling logs now. I see many sampler events labeled `seed_rotated` and a handful where `top_p` is `null` in the serialized payload: `sampler: params={"temp":0.7,"top_p":null,"top_k":0}`
liam: If top_p is null what does runtime do? fallback -> greedy? treat as 1.0?
sasha: Current runtime treats None/null as 1.0 (i.e. no nucleus). In combination with top_k=0 on quant model this increases variance — repro locally: top_p=1.0,temp=0.7,seed=42 reproduces bad output.
nora: Can you grep for serializer changes in the PR? Also check seed cache flushes — I saw a cache flush around 03:39AM in deploy logs.
sasha: Found it: PR #2896 changed SamplingConfig JSON serializer to drop keys with value==None. The serializer has a bug where it mutates the object when called multiple times due to in-place filtering + caching. So some requests end up without top_p key.
maya: That would explain sudden drift. Quick mitigation: revert serializer change in canary and re-run subset.
liam: Spinning canary with revert now and will run a 1k-sample ablation on cs-suite. ETA ~20m.
eval-bot: nightly-eval | model=redwood-6b-quant | suite=cs-suite | drop 0.62->0.27 | alert_id=20240312-0912
nora: Also note seed rotation: a handful of requests have seed==0 logged after cache flush, looks like uninitialized seed reused which amplifies nondeterminism. We should ensure seed default is explicit.
sasha: Proposed patch: avoid mutating SamplingConfig in serializer, return a shallow copy, and serialize top_p explicitly as 1.0 when absent to avoid ambiguity. Also add a test that serializing twice doesn't change the object.
maya: Sounds good. If canary recovers metrics we ship patch and schedule a full-night rerun. Also open incident ticket and notify any customers that might have seen flakiness. cc: @product-alerts
liam: Canary pre-run results: preliminary mean 0.59 — much improved from 0.27. Full 1k run finishing now, will post link.
eval-bot: rerun-complete | model=redwood-6b-quant | suite=cs-suite | mean=0.60 | link=https://internal.redwood/evals/1745012345/rerun
maya: Great. We'll cut the patch PR and merge after tests. Thanks all.
